title: Bubble and Squeak
subtitle: Fried potato and cabbage cake
excerpt: Leftover mashed potato and cooked cabbage or sprouts, formed into patties and fried in butter until deeply golden and crisp on both sides. The classic British way to use up Boxing Day leftovers.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bubble and squeak has been a British kitchen staple since the 18th century, named for the sounds the vegetables make in the pan. Originally it contained meat as well as vegetables. By the Victorian era the modern version, made from fried potato and cabbage, had become standard. It is most commonly made the day after a roast dinner using leftover vegetables. The mixture is shaped into a large cake or individual patties and fried until a proper crust forms on both sides.

content.text: The mixture should be firm enough to hold its shape when pressed into patties. If it is too wet, add a tablespoon of flour. The crust only forms properly if the patties are left without moving for 4 to 5 minutes per side: resist the urge to prod or shift them. Serve with leftover cold cuts, fried eggs, or as a side to a full English breakfast.

items.preparation: cooked and roughly chopped, or cooked sprouts, halved

content.text: Fry the onion in half the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft and golden. Remove from the pan.
Combine the mashed potato, cooked cabbage, and fried onion in a bowl. Season well with salt and pepper. Divide into 8 equal portions. Shape each into a patty about 1.5 cm thick.

Melt the remaining butter in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the patties. Cook without moving for 4 to 5 minutes until a deep golden crust forms on the underside. Flip carefully and cook for a further 4 to 5 minutes until the second side is equally golden. Serve immediately.
